chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Maysami, from Hisham ibn Ahmar and Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: Three people will be punished on the Day of Resurrection. One is the one who makes an image of an animal; he will be punished until he breathes life into it, but he is not one who breathes life into it. The one who fabricates (false) dreams will be punished until he ties together two grains of barley, but he is not one who ties them together. The one who eavesdrops on people's conversation while they dislike it for him, molten lead (or solder) will be poured into his ear, and that is the 'Asrab'.

key_terms.الْأَسْرَبُ: The specific name for the molten lead poured in the ear

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people punished on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual consequences of three specific acts: image-making, dream fabrication, and eavesdropping, where the punishment intricately mirrors the action yet emphasizes a state of inability or imperfection. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *tashbih* (resembling God’s creation) and *ghibah* (eavesdropping) as distinct sins with unique eschatological penalties. The metaphorical punishments highlight the transient nature of these acts compared to the eternal reality of the Hereafter.
